text: Wardrobe with gliding mirrored doors

text: Dining table with butterfly leaf, seats 6-10

text: Teak bench for the patio

text: Tall freestanding dressing mirror
note: Freestanding rules out Wall Mirror, and the word dressing does not make it a Dressing Table.

text: Fridge freezer

text: Fitted kitchen worktop

text: How would you rate the front desk staff?
How satisfied were you with housekeeping during your stay?
How was the food in our restaurant?
How would you rate your spa treatment?
Were your towels changed daily?
How quick was check-in when you arrived?
Was the breakfast buffet well stocked?
Did the air conditioning and the shower work properly throughout your stay?
How likely are you to recommend our hotel to a friend?
note: An overall loyalty question that is about no single department.

text: Was your room clean, and was everything in it in working order when you arrived?
note: Cleanliness is Housekeeping and working order is Maintenance; neither is named.

text: How easy was it to book your stay on our website?
note: Online booking happens before arrival and involves none of the listed departments, including Front Desk.

text: When you reported the broken TV to reception, how quickly was it logged and then repaired?
note: Reception logging the report is Front Desk and the repair is Maintenance.

text: How did you first discover our product?
How easy was it to complete your purchase?
Was your delivery on time?
How likely are you to renew your subscription?
Did the agent resolve your issue on the first contact?
How helpful was the setup wizard in getting you started?
Where did you first hear about us?
How smooth was checkout, and did your parcel arrive when promised?
note: Checkout is the Purchase stage and parcel arrival is Delivery; neither tag word appears.

text: Did the welcome call cover everything you needed, and have you had to contact the helpdesk since?
note: A welcome call is Onboarding and contacting the helpdesk is Support.

text: Thinking about ordering, shipping and getting set up: which step was the most frustrating?
note: Three stages are named by paraphrase: ordering, shipping and getting set up.

text: What is your age group?
note: A demographic question about no journey stage.

text: Overall, how satisfied are you with our company?
note: Overall satisfaction is not tied to any one stage.

text: I have confidence in the senior leadership of this company.
I am satisfied with my pay and benefits.
My workload is manageable.
I see opportunities for career growth here.
I receive recognition when I do good work.
My colleagues and I cooperate well to get things done.
My salary is fair compared with similar roles elsewhere.
I have the equipment and software I need to do my job.
People of all backgrounds are treated fairly here.
I can see a path to promotion in this organisation.
I would recommend this company as a great place to work.
note: An overall advocacy item that measures engagement itself, not any one driver.

text: How many years have you worked here?
note: A tenure question; length of service is not Career Growth.

text: Executives set a clear direction and celebrate employees' achievements.
note: Executives setting direction is Leadership and celebrating achievements is Recognition.

text: My workload would be manageable if our systems weren't so slow and outdated.
note: The statement ties workload to poor systems, so both drivers apply.

text: I'm fairly paid, but there is nowhere for me to progress to.
note: Covers pay and lack of progression; the second half is negated but still about Career Growth.

text: How long did you wait before being seen?
How would you rate the cleanliness of your room?
Was your pain well managed during your stay?
How easy was it to book your appointment?
How would you rate the quality of the food?
Did the nurses treat you with respect and kindness?
Did the physician explain your diagnosis in a way you could understand?
Was the invoice you received accurate and easy to understand?
Were you given clear instructions about what to do after going home?
Did the pharmacist explain what your new tablets were for and their possible side effects?
note: An explanation, but given by a pharmacist about tablets, so Medication and not Doctor Communication.

text: Were conversations about your condition held where other patients could not overhear?
note: It asks where conversations took place, not how well anything was explained, so Privacy only.

text: Were the reception staff polite, and were you seen at your scheduled time?
note: Politeness is Staff Courtesy and being seen on time is Wait Times; making the booking is not asked about.

text: Were the bathrooms kept spotless, and were your meals served hot?
note: Two themes by paraphrase: spotless bathrooms and hot meals.

text: Was it easy to get through on the phone to arrange your visit, and to park once you got here?
note: Arranging the visit by phone is Appointment Booking and the second half is Parking.

text: Would you recommend this hospital to friends and family?
note: An overall recommendation question tied to no theme.

text: Which ward were you admitted to?
note: A profiling question, not an experience theme.

text: How easy is the product to use?
How satisfied are you with our customer support?
How would you rate the mobile app?
How useful are the reporting dashboards?
How helpful is our documentation?
How quickly do pages load for you?
Is the product good value for what you pay?
How well does the product connect with the other tools you use?
Do you get too many email alerts from us?
How often does the product crash or become unavailable?
Is there anything you wish the product could do that it can't today?
Were your invoices correct and charged on the right date?
note: About invoice accuracy and charge timing, not how much the product costs, so Billing and not Pricing.

text: Does the product work with your screen reader and keyboard-only navigation?
note: Assistive-technology support is Accessibility, not general Ease of Use or Integrations.

text: Did your existing spreadsheets upload correctly when you first set up your account?
note: Uploading existing data is Data Import and first account setup is Onboarding.

text: Can you find the right record fast, and are results returned without delay?
note: Finding records is Search and results without delay is Speed.

text: Is the phone version as fast and stable as the desktop one?
note: Phone version is Mobile App, fast is Speed and stable is Reliability.

text: Does the help centre explain how to set up single sign-on and two-factor authentication?
note: Help-centre articles are Documentation and the subject, sign-in protection, is Security.

text: Can you change the colours, layout and fields to suit your team's workflow?
note: Asks whether the user can change things, not whether the look is good, so Customisation and not Visual Design.

text: How likely are you to recommend us to a colleague?
note: An overall recommendation question about no specific theme.

text: What is your job role?
note: A profiling question about the respondent, not the product.
